item.description:

An implementation of the TLS/SSL protocols

Release Summary

  • The 20261021 security policies (TLS12_20261021_1 and TLS10_20261021_1 through TLS10_20261021_4) no longer offer the SHA-1 signature schemes rsa_pkcs1_sha1 and ecdsa_sha1.
  • TLS 1.3 clients that send an X25519MLKEM768 key share and prefer X25519 as their classical curve now reuse the hybrid's X25519 key for the classical key share. This saves one key generation per ClientHello. The groups offered are unchanged.
  • s2n_set_server_name now fully replaces a previously set server name. Before, setting a shorter name left the end of the old name in place.
  • If s2n_connection_set_config fails, the connection keeps its previous hostname verification callback and no longer switches to the new config's callback.
  • There is no new Rust bindings release with this version. The Rust bindings changes in this range, including the revert of the default record size change (#6167), were already released in s2n-tls 0.3.48 (#6168; s2n-tls, s2n-tls-tokio, s2n-tls-sys). s2n-tls-sys 0.3.48 already vendors the C changes listed above.

FLOSS kanban, built with Meteor. Official Public Support at GitHub issues only. Official Private Pre-Paid Support at https://wekan.fi/commercial-support/ only. Translation PRs to imports/i18n/data/en.i18n.json, other translations at https://app.transifex.com/wekan/wekan . No telemetry.

In short

The file-integrity scan stops reporting attachments and
avatars that WeKan deleted itself as missing, which had buried real
StorageBleed findings under thousands of false ones. The recurring-checklist
reset no longer scans every checklist on each tick. In the REST API, a
refused custom-field update changes nothing, ownership transfer takes only the
boards the user administers, and deleting a missing integration answers 404.

Thanks to above GitHub users for their contributions.

More details at ChangeLog

item.description:
robolectric/robolectric | 6086 stars| 1393 forks.

| Java | Shell | Starlark | Kotlin |

Android Unit Testing Framework

Robolectric 4.18 adds Linux arm64 support to the native runtime, supports native resources on SDK 36 and above, and contains many performance improvements and bug fixes.

If you have any issues, please file them here.

Breaking Changes

  • Support for SDK 23 has been removed. The minimum supported SDK is now 24, matching AndroidX (#11604).
  • The shadows-httpclient module has been removed. It was deprecated in 4.17, and org.apache.http is no longer instrumented (#11373, #11544).
  • @TextLayoutMode has been removed. Realistic text layout, the default since 2019, is now always used (#11498).
  • ShadowRemoteCallbackList has been removed, as the real RemoteCallbackList works without it (#11368).
  • HttpResponseCache.install() now also sets ResponseCache.getDefault(), as it does on a device (#11493).

Linux arm64 support

Robolectric's native runtime now includes Linux arm64 (aarch64) native libraries, so tests that use native SQLite (the default) and native graphics (@GraphicsMode(NATIVE)) can run on Linux arm64 environments, such as GitHub's ubuntu-24.04-arm runners, AWS Graviton machines, and arm64 Docker containers on Apple silicon. No configuration is needed (#11625, #11633). As on Apple silicon, the legacy SQLite mode (SQLiteMode.Mode.LEGACY) isn't supported on Linux arm64.

Other Highlights

  • Native resources (ResourcesMode.NATIVE) now work on SDK 36 and above, not only SDK 36 (#11578).
  • Robolectric no longer prints the "restricted method in java.lang.System has been called" warnings on JDK 24+ (#11482).
  • The shadow annotation processor now supports KSP (#10996).
  • Lots of performance improvements:
    • Resource values are shared between bags and themes instead of copied (#11726, #11595)
    • Faster shadow method lookups (#11723, #11593)
    • Cached resource reference resolution (#11586)
    • Cached service and plugin lookups (#11451, #11594, #11631)
    • Native runtime assets are extracted once and shared (#11453, #11522)
    • Faster class loading checks in the sandbox (#11662)
    • Regexes compiled once instead of on every use (#11399, #11400, #11401)
  • Conscrypt is now enabled by default on Mac arm64 (#11352).

item.title: [gohugoio/hugo] v0.170.0
item.description:
gohugoio/hugo | 90470 stars| 8444 forks.

| Go | Shell | HTML | Dockerfile | CSS | JavaScript | Makefile | C | Go Template |

The world’s fastest framework for building websites.

The big change in this release is that the extended edition of Hugo is gone. LibSass has been deprecated for a long time, and it was the main reason we needed a CGO-enabled extended build. There is now only one Hugo binary, and apart from LibSass it has all the features the extended build had.

Notes

  • Setting transpiler to libsass in css.Sass now returns an error. Dart Sass is now the default and the only transpiler, so you need to install it if you use Sass.
  • We no longer publish hugo_extended_* archives. To avoid breaking existing CI setups, we publish aliases for the most downloaded extended archives (e.g. hugo_extended_<version>_linux-amd64.tar.gz, hugo_extended_<version>_Linux-64bit.tar.gz, the linux-amd64.deb, linux-arm64.tar.gz and windows-amd64.zip), but you should update your scripts to use the standard archives. The extended_withdeploy builds are also removed. See Installation.
  • hugo.IsExtended now always returns false, and the module config setting hugoVersion.extended is deprecated and has no effect.
  • Command-line flags (e.g. --buildDrafts) now override OS environment variables (e.g. HUGO_BUILDDRAFTS). This also fixes HUGO_ENVIRONMENT=qa hugo build -e staging loading the staging config but reporting qa in hugo.Environment.
  • strings.Truncate has been rewritten on top of a proper HTML scanner. It now handles comments, void elements, quoted attributes with > and raw text elements such as script correctly, and it's faster and allocates less. On a curious note, the old version was implemented by Mathias Biilmann, the Netlify CEO.
  • time.Time values now keep their named time zone, and eq, ne, in and uniq compare time.Time values by instant.
  • resources.Match and friends now preserve the directory casing in the matched paths, so e.g. resources.Match "gallery/Travel/Iceland/*" now works on case-sensitive file systems.
  • Syncing of static files is much faster for big unchanged files, as we now skip the content check for files with the same size and modification time.
  • Several fixes and hardening of the WASM based image codecs (AVIF crash at encoderSpeed 6 and lower, recovering from broken WASM instances in the server).

Security

Hugo

  • Passthrough content is now HTML escaped when no passthrough render hook is set, unless markup.goldmark.renderer.unsafe is enabled. Before this, e.g. \(<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>\) in a content file emitted raw HTML.
  • The wrapperClass option, settable from the highlight shortcode and transform.Highlight, is now escaped.
  • Vendored module paths are now restricted to the _vendor directory (symlinks pointing outside are rejected).

Thanks to @R0X4R for finding and reporting the last two issues.

Go

This release is built with Go 1.27.4, which includes 12 security fixes. The one most relevant for Hugo is a crash in the net/http HTTP/1 server (used by hugo server) caused by a race in MaxBytesReader. The other 11 are in the cmd/go toolchain (cgo flag and linker injection at build time) and mainly matter if you build Hugo from source with untrusted dependencies.

The controller is now built with the Go 1.27.4 toolchain (from 1.26.10) and golang.org/x/net v0.62.0 (from v0.60.0), picking up the security fixes in the Go standard library and x/net that those releases carry. x/net is linked into the controller binary, so the rebuild reaches the released image. Supporting golang.org/x/{crypto,sync,sys,term,text,tools} modules were bumped along with it. No change to controller behavior or configuration. (#4952, @shraddhabang)

Controller image rebuilt on a newer base image
The controller image is now built on eks-distro-minimal-base-nonroot:2026-11-10-1794337279.2023 (from 2026-10-23-1792785692.2023), picking up the latest OS-package security fixes in the EKS-D minimal base. This is an image rebuild only; there is no change to controller behavior or configuration. (#4952, @shraddhabang)

🔧 Enhancements and Fixes

Helm chart

  • Add matchConditions support to the Service webhook so it only fires for the Service objects it cares about (a good default is object.spec.type == 'LoadBalancer'). This lets users create other Service objects even when the webhook is unavailable, and removes a cyclical dependency during cluster bootstrap. (#4828, @BojanZelic-DD)

Endpoints

  • Populate PodEndpoint.NodeReadyTime for ready endpoints whose node is Ready, not only for not-ready endpoints admitted on a Ready node. When a node flaps Ready → NotReady → Ready, the kubelet restores the pod's Ready condition with its original LastTransitionTime, so consumers measuring target-registration latency previously saw the pod's age (hours to days) for these re-registrations. Failing to read the node leaves NodeReadyTime zero (logged at V(1)); the endpoint is still returned, and endpoint selection is unchanged. (#4941, @zac-nixon)

Security groups

  • Log security group ingress authorize/revoke failures at error level, including the security group ID, in AuthorizeSGIngress/RevokeSGIngress and in the per-security-group reconcile loop. Previously these failures were invisible in the controller logs and could only be found through CloudTrail, which made a shared-backend-SG failure that stalled reconciliation of multiple TargetGroupBindings hard to diagnose. Errors still propagate exactly as before; this only makes the existing failures observable. Fixes #3809. (#4924, @avneetbansal-aws)

  • ZipDirectoryEntry#exportFileSystemHandle() now aborts and unlocks the destination file stream when reading an entry fails before its data is written, e.g. on a wrong password or a corrupted entry. Previously the stream opened for that entry was left open and locked
  • ZipDirectoryEntry#addFileSystemEntry() now rejects when reading a nested directory fails, e.g. on a permission error. Previously the error surfaced as an unhandled rejection and the returned promise never settled
  • ZipFileEntry#getData() now accepts a bare WritableStream, as declared, instead of throwing "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'getWriter')"; an object exposing a writable property keeps working

Type declarations

  • Reader#readUint8Array(), Writer#writeUint8Array(), Writer#getData() and the init() methods now declare that they may return synchronously, which is what Uint8ArrayReader, Uint8ArrayWriter and Data64URIWriter do. A custom reader or writer implemented synchronously now type-checks, and calling .then() on these methods is no longer accepted by TypeScript since it fails at runtime on the synchronous classes: use await instead. The classes implemented asynchronously, e.g. TextWriter and BlobWriter, keep their promise-only declarations
  • ZipWriterStream#transform() and ZipWriterStream#writable() are now typed on Uint8Array chunks on both sides and no longer take a type parameter: the readable side of transform() is the zipped stream, never the type of the input chunks

  • msDosCompatible: Info-ZIP unzip builds without Unicode support, e.g. the one shipped with macOS, fail to extract entries with non-ASCII names when the MS-DOS platform is declared, whatever the language encoding flag says
  • The ZipWriterStream examples now encode their strings with a TextEncoderStream: the streams piped into the instance must carry Uint8Array chunks
  • A lazily-read Blob from fs.openAsBlob() or Bun.file() must be wrapped in a BlobReader; the two passages saying it could be passed directly to ZipReader were wrong
  • passThrough: "compressed": two encrypted entries holding the same content read identical only when the content was compressed identically; different compressed data does not prove different content
  • useUnicodeFileNames: false: ZipReader decodes the resulting UTF-8 names correctly since it detects valid UTF-8 when the flag is clear; the readers that trust the flag, e.g. Python zipfile and Info-ZIP unzip, do not
  • ZipDirectoryEntry#exportWritable() resolves to the WritableStream instance, not to a Uint8Array as its description said

item.title: [ponylang/ponyc] 0.78.2
item.description:
ponylang/ponyc | 6221 stars| 440 forks.

| C++ | C | GAP | Shell | Pony | CMake | Dockerfile | PowerShell | Python | Nix |

Pony is an open-source, actor-model, capabilities-secure, high performance programming language

Fix building on 32-bit

The runtime failed to compile on 32-bit ARM with GCC 8.3 due to two issues: implicit narrowing conversions from int to uint16_t in actor batch-size arithmetic, and a call to gettid() whose glibc wrapper is only available in glibc 2.30 and later.

The narrowing conversions are caused by C integer promotion: compound assignments like batch_size -= 25 promote both operands to int, and the implicit conversion back to uint16_t triggers -Werror=conversion. The gettid() call is replaced with syscall(SYS_gettid), which works on all glibc versions.

Add i386 (32-bit x86) support to the embedded LLD linker

The embedded LLD linker can now link Pony programs targeting 32-bit x86 Linux (i386/i686). Previously, compiling for an i386 target failed at link time with "unsupported architecture for embedded LLD." The embedded linker already supported 32-bit ARM; this extends the same support to 32-bit x86, covering both musl and glibc systems.

Fix PosixDate on 32-bit

On systems with 32-bit time_t (such as 32-bit ARM Linux), every PosixDate produced wrong field values regardless of the input. PosixDate(0, 0) returned year 1905 instead of 1970, and time() returned -2037645953 instead of 0.

The upper bound for dates is now clamped to the time_t range on each platform. On 32-bit time_t systems, this means the maximum representable date is 2038-01-19 03:14:07 UTC (the Y2038 limit) rather than year 2147483647.

Fix short-circuit and/or dropping side effects when left operand is a compile-time constant

When the left operand of a short-circuit and or or folded to a compile-time constant, ponyc dropped the code that computed it. Any side effects in that left operand — assignments, field writes — never ran, and the program silently produced wrong results.

var x: U32 = 1
let r = ((x = x + 1; true) and (x > 2))
// x was 1 (the assignment never ran); now x is 2

A related shape — a nested short-circuit that folds to a constant, used as the left operand of an outer and or or — crashed the compiler instead of producing a wrong answer.

Fix F64.min() and F64.max() on ARM32

F64.min() and F64.max() returned incorrect results on ARM32 — both returned the maximum of their two arguments regardless of which was called. They now produce correct results, preserving IEEE 754-2019 minimum/maximum semantics for NaN and signed zero.

Fix incorrect constant folding of I128 division and shift operations

Constant I128 division and remainder gave wrong results when the divisor was a 128-bit value whose low 64 bits were all ones — for example, 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF (which is 2^64−1, not −1). Such divisors were truncated to −1, producing the signed-overflow result instead of the actual quotient.

// Before: d was I128.min_value(), r was 0
// After: d and r are both -9223372036854775808
let d: I128 = I128.min_value() / 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF
let r: I128 = I128.min_value() % 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF

Constant 128-bit shift amounts above 2^64 were also accepted when they should have been rejected as exceeding the type width.

// Before: compiled without error, produced undefined behavior
// After: "shift amount greater than type width" compile error
let a: U128 = 1 << 0x1_0000_0000_0000_0005

Fix ponyc -r=ir writing builtin's IR over the program's IR

When emitting LLVM IR with -r=ir, ponyc wrote both the program's module and builtin's module to the same .main.ll file. Builtin was written second, so the file contained only builtin's definitions — the program's IR was lost. Each module is now written to a distinct file: <name>.main.ll for the program and <name>.builtin.ll for builtin.

Fix user package named main colliding with program module at link

A program with a sub-package in a directory named main (or Main, MAIN, or any other casing) failed to link. The compiler assigned duplicate .bc filenames to the user package and the program's own module, producing a linker error. The compiler now detects the collision and disambiguates the user package's filename.

Fix time functions truncating to 32 bits on 32-bit musl Linux

On 32-bit musl Linux (such as Alpine on i386 or ARM), Time.seconds(), Time.now(), and file timestamp operations (FilePath.set_time, Directory.set_time_at, File.set_time) silently truncated time values to 32 bits. File timestamps past January 2038 wrapped to negative values, and after 2038, Time.seconds() and Time.now() would return wrong results.

musl defines time_t as 64-bit on all architectures, but the plain C symbol names (time, clock_gettime, utimes, futimes, futimesat) are 32-bit compatibility wrappers on 32-bit targets. C code compiled with musl's headers gets the 64-bit versions automatically; Pony's FFI declarations bypassed the headers and bound the 32-bit wrappers directly.

Time values now use the full 64-bit range on 32-bit musl. On glibc 32-bit systems, time_t is still 32 bits at the C level, so the Y2038 limit remains there — that is a glibc constraint, not a Pony one.

Fix floating-point arithmetic giving wrong results on 32-bit x86 without SSE2

On 32-bit x86 targets whose CPU lacked SSE2, floating-point arithmetic could produce incorrect results that violated IEEE 754. ponyc now unconditionally enables SSE2 for all 32-bit x86 targets.

Fix link failure on x86-64 when passing --features=-cx16

The Pony runtime uses 128-bit atomic operations that need the x86-64 cx16 CPU feature. ponyc turns that feature on for x86-64 targets, but passing --features=-cx16 turned it off and ponyc didn't turn it back on. The compiled program then referenced __atomic_compare_exchange_16, and on platforms where nothing provides that function, such as macOS, linking failed with an undefined symbol. ponyc now keeps cx16 on for every x86-64 target, even when --features turns it off.

Fix misaligned loads and stores in Array[U8] multi-byte accessors

Array[U8]'s multi-byte methods (read_u16 through read_u128, update_u16 through update_u128, and push_u16 through push_u128) generated loads and stores assuming the wider type's alignment at an arbitrary byte offset. On i386 with SSE2, the u128 operations crashed with a segfault at unaligned offsets; buffered.Reader and buffered.Writer u128 operations crashed the same way. On other targets the operations could silently produce wrong results, even when they didn't crash.

The twelve methods now work correctly at any byte offset.

Fix integer overflow in Array[U8] multi-byte bounds checks

Array[U8]'s multi-byte read and update methods (read_u16 through read_u128, update_u16 through update_u128) accepted offsets that should have been rejected. An offset near USize.max_value() bypassed the bounds check and read or wrote arbitrary memory outside the array instead of raising an error.

Add NixOS linking support

ponyc's embedded linker can now link Pony programs on NixOS when run inside nix-shell or nix develop. Previously, linking failed because NixOS places libc, GCC runtime libraries, and system headers under /nix/store instead of the standard /usr/lib and /usr/include paths that ponyc searches.

When the NIX_CC environment variable points to a Nix compiler wrapper with a nix-support/ directory, ponyc reads the dynamic linker path from nix-support/dynamic-linker, extracts library directories from NIX_LDFLAGS, reads the glibc prefix from nix-support/orig-libc (for CRT startup objects), reads compiler runtime library paths from nix-support/cc-ldflags (for libgcc/libgcc_s), and extracts system include directories from NIX_CFLAGS_COMPILE. These paths are used for CRT object discovery, GCC runtime discovery, the ELF dynamic linker (PT_INTERP), -L/-rpath link flags, and C shim include paths. On macOS with nix-darwin, only library search paths are added.

If ponyc detects it is running on NixOS without the Nix environment variables set, it prints a diagnostic suggesting nix-shell or nix develop.

Report an error for malformed --features and invalid --cpu values

Some bad --features and --cpu values crashed ponyc partway through compiling instead of producing an error. A --features string with an empty entry, such as --features=+sse4.2,, or with an entry that doesn't start with + or -, such as --features=cx16 or "--features=+sse4.2, +avx", aborted with the same LLVM message printed hundreds of times. On x86-64, a --cpu name that wasn't a processor for the target, such as --cpu=bogus or the 32-bit-only --cpu=athlon-xp, stopped with an LLVM fatal error. On RISC-V, a CPU for the other bit width, such as --cpu=generic-rv32 with a 64-bit triple, also stopped with an LLVM fatal error.

ponyc now checks both options before it compiles anything and prints an error that names the bad value. For --features, ponyc checks that each entry is non-empty and starts with + or -; it doesn't check which features are being turned on or off.

Error:
invalid --features value "cx16": feature "cx16" must start with '+' or '-'

Error:
invalid --cpu value "bogus": not a recognized processor for target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu

An empty --features= and an empty --cpu= are still accepted. A feature name that LLVM doesn't know, such as +notafeature, is still accepted with a warning, as before.

Some --cpu values that used to be accepted are now errors:

  • On targets other than x86, such as ARM, AArch64, and RISC-V, an unrecognized --cpu name used to print an LLVM warning and build for the target's default processor. It is now rejected.
  • On x86, --cpu=generic is now rejected. It already failed for any program with C shims. To build for the baseline x86-64 processor, use --cpu=x86-64.
  • On RISC-V, --cpu=generic and other names that only set tuning, such as rocket, are now rejected. Use --cpu=generic-rv64 or --cpu=generic-rv32 instead.
  • On every target, --cpu=help is now rejected instead of printing LLVM's CPU list.

Fix integer overflow in Array.copy_from and Array.copy_to bounds arithmetic

Passing a large index to Array.copy_from or Array.copy_to could write past the end of the destination array's allocation. copy_from could also read past the end of the source array.

Fix crashes when disabling required x86-64 CPU features

On x86-64, passing --features=-sse, -sse2, -64bit, or -64bit-mode could crash the compiler or fail during linking. ponyc now keeps these required features enabled, even when --features requests disabling them. This follows the existing behavior for cx16 on x86-64 and sse2 on 32-bit x86.

Fix integer overflow in Array.concat and Array.append bounds arithmetic

Passing a large len to Array.concat could write past the end of the array's allocation. Array.append had the same vulnerability when the array was already large.

Report fileless compiler errors without invalid diagnostic URIs

The language server now reports compiler errors that have no source file as editor messages, including their related explanations. These errors no longer appear as document diagnostics under invalid URIs such as file://.

Preserve runtime tracing across thread startup and category changes

Runtime-enabled tracing could stop recording events when a runtime thread started or when category changes reached schedulers at different times. Tracing now remains enabled or disabled according to the latest category change.

item.title: [smithy-lang/smithy] Smithy CLI v1.75.0
item.description:
smithy-lang/smithy | 2396 stars| 265 forks.

| Java | Shell | Dockerfile | Smithy | Batchfile | Makefile | Python | Kotlin |

Smithy is a protocol-agnostic interface definition language and set of tools for generating clients, servers, and documentation for any programming language.

1.75.0 (2026-11-09)

Features

  • Bumped the IDL version to 2.1.
    (#3059)
  • Added the new idx trait to declare the expected wire order of a shape's
    members as well as the new indexed trait to declare that every structure and
    union in the closure of a service MUST be indexed.
    (#3238)
  • Added inline collection declarations to IDL 2.1, allowing list and map shapes
    to be declared directly in member target positions using [Target] and
    {KeyTarget: ValueTarget} instead of a separate top-level shape. The
    assembler generates one shared synthetic shape per distinct collection type in
    a namespace. (#3134)
  • Added aws.apigateway#apiGatewayConfig trait, which defines the API Gateway
    configuration version for a service.
    (#3315)
  • Added tagged string literals to IDL 2.1. Prefixing a string or text block with
    #re, #b, #hex, or #timestamp changes how its content is interpreted at
    parse time, making regular expressions, binary data, hex dumps, and RFC 3339
    timestamps easier to write and read.
    (#3163)
  • Added syntax sugar for idx traits so that indexes can be defined more
    concisely. Models serialized with SmithyIdlModelSerializer will use this
    syntax by default and the Smithy formatter will update IDL 2.1+ models to use
    it. (#3238)
  • Added the unstable @discriminated trait for modeling unions that are
    serialized as internally tagged objects in JSON, along with validation that
    members target structures and that the discriminator does not collide with a
    targeted structure member. Support for the trait is optional.
    (#3343)
  • Add since field for unstableFeatureInfo and explain for downgrade in diff
    event (#3316)
  • Added support for setting a model to a bare major version, which will then
    resolve to the latest minor version of that major version. For example, "2"
    will resolve to "2.1".
    (#3367)

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed flattening mixins so that when a shape uses multiple mixins that apply
    the same trait, the trait from the mixin that appears later in the list takes
    precedence, matching how traits are resolved when a model is loaded.
    (#3349)
  • Stop treating the source location given to ModelAssembler#addUnparsedModel
    as a JAR to import. In-memory models with a .jar source location are now
    ignored with a warning. Use addImport to load JARs.
    (#3323)
  • Fix quadratic-time duplicate detection in the @uniqueItems node validator.
    (#3338)
  • Report resource mixins that define properties as a validation event instead of
    throwing an IllegalStateException from the model assembler.
    (#3350)
  • Fixed Smithy IDL serialization of member and inline collection targets that
    reference public prelude shapes omitted from a programmatically built model.
  • Fixed FileManifest path validation so that paths containing .. segments
    can no longer escape the manifest's base directory.
    (#3334)
  • Improved performance when merging repeated array metadata values, which now
    scales linearly instead of quadratically.
    (#3344)
  • Fixed super-linear regex backtracking when validating enum member and trait
    names, enum values, CloudWatch namespaces, ARN templates, and endpoint
    patterns, and when formatting generated trait Javadoc. Most of the affected
    regular expressions were replaced with linear scans.
    (#3336)
  • Only load source context for validation events from local files and JARs.
    (#3322)

Documentation

  • Clarified that the order of values in concatenated list traits and metadata
    arrays is unspecified, and documented how ModelAssembler handles repeated
    shapes and metadata added in code.
    (#3363)

Other

  • Added negative event stream protocol tests for oversized string headers,
    covering both single-byte ASCII overflow and multibyte UTF-8 byte-limit
    overflow. (#3325)

The OpenEXR project provides the specification and reference implementation of the EXR file format, the professional-grade image storage format of the motion picture industry.

Patch release that addresses several build and security issues, and also fixes a regression introduced in v3.3.0 that leads to excessive memory usage during write, especially with DWA compression (Issue #2791).

  • Fix a configuration issue with OpenJPH 0.33.0 that caused it to silently and incorrectly fall back to the vendored version (PR #2813)
  • The vendored OpenJPH is now built in a custom namespace to avoid symbol collision with other versions when built statically (2811) built statically,
  • The vendored OpenJPH version is now 0.33.0.

  • OPENEXR_USE_INTERNAL_IMATH/OPENJPH are are now included in OpenEXRConfig.h alongside OPENEXR_USE_INTERNAL_DEFLATE/ZSTD.
  • 32-bit glibc builds now guarantee support for files of size 2GiB or more (2812)

This release addresses the following security vulnerabilities:

  • CVE Pending (GHSA-PP92-4RV3-WFQ6) OpenEXR: a signed-int data-window-origin overflow in the OpenEXRUtil Image API turns Imf::loadImage into an attacker-steered out-of-bounds write
  • CVE Pending (GHSA-2V77-PVHX-25C3) Integer overflow in legacy OpenEXR.OutputFile.writePixels() causes heap over-read
